specificSetting: consumption and environmental responsibility planning brief 16

tasks.scenario: Two source texts debate whether convenient recycling services encourage genuine responsibility or merely pacify consumers.
tasks.purpose: Synthesise competing claims, evaluate assumptions, and develop an independent position on the tension between convenience and responsibility.
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Source texts use original framing (convenience vs. moral effort; psychological cost of waste). No reuse of Test 01 structures or phrases.

tasks.scenario: Review of a local recycling service for a specialist magazine, evaluating balance between convenience and waste reduction.
tasks.purpose: Assess effectiveness of the service and recommend a change to increase long-term responsibility.
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Review genre with concrete audience (environmental officers). No overlap with Test 01 review (book review for literary magazine).

tasks.scenario: Report for a municipal waste authority analysing how convenience affects long-term environmental behaviour.
tasks.purpose: Analyse implications of current design and propose an action to encourage personal responsibility.
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Report genre with specific institutional audience. No similarity to Test 01 report (jobs fair).

tasks.scenario: Article for an online magazine arguing whether convenience or responsibility should be prioritised in recycling services.
tasks.purpose: Explain a position, describe a consequence, suggest implementation, and request a follow-up discussion.
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Article with direct request to magazine for follow-up. No reuse of Test 01 article structure (travel alternatives).
